context: The input is choices = [1, 1, 2] at indices 0, 1, and 2. “First 1” and “second 1” distinguish indices 0 and 1. The figure marks the second 1 with a hat to identify it. Both have numerical value 1.
description: Two constraints track indices and values separately. The array selected tracks indices used on the current path. The set duplicated in the code below tracks values actually chosen in the current round after the selected check. Each recursive call creates its own duplicated. Backtracking restores selected and state but retains values already tried in the current call’s set.

The figure marks only two same-round pruning decisions: skipping the second 1 at root [] and after prefix [2]. The table of choices by prefix gives the decisions at all six nonterminal prefixes. Its column for used indices follows from the code and does not correspond to pruning marks in the figure. The table of three distinct permutations gives both the element identities and the resulting values at each leaf.

frames.explanation: A path can choose both 1s in succession because they have distinct indices. Within any one round, only one branch is expanded for the value 1.
frames.title: Pruning equal choices in the same round

summary: Try the value 1 only once in a round to prune duplicate subtrees before exploring them.
